name: Feni
tagline: A small southeastern district on the Tripura border — the Muhuri sluice and the country's first wind turbines, ancient legend-soaked dighis, Mughal mosques, and the birthplace of filmmaker Zahir Raihan.

guide.bestTime: November to February — cool, dry weather for the Muhuri Project sunsets, the dighis and the old mosques. The coast at Sonagazi is most pleasant out of the monsoon.
guide.gettingThere: On the Dhaka–Chittagong highway and main rail line — Feni Junction is a stop for most southbound trains, and Mohipal is the town's bus hub. The Muhuri Project is ~18 km south at Sonagazi; Chand Gazi mosque and Shamsher Gazi's country lie east in Chhagalnaiya.
guide.difficulty: Easy — flat roads and short CNG/bus hops. A couple of sites (Sharshadi, Shamsher Gazi) are rural; ask locally for directions.

mustVisit.name: Muhuri Project (Irrigation Regulator)
mustVisit.description: A vast closure dam and 40-gate regulator where the Feni, Muhuri and Kalidas-Pahaliya rivers meet — ringed by an embankment, water-hyacinth lagoons and Bangladesh's first wind turbines. The district's premier nature outing and a favourite winter picnic and sunset spot.
mustVisit.history: The regulator and Feni River closure dam were built in 1982 for irrigation and flood control; the country's first wind-power unit — four 225 kW turbines — was installed here in 2004–05.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 18 km south of Feni town, Sonagazi Upazila

tips: Go for sunset over the water and turbines
Carry your own food and water — facilities on site are limited

mustVisit.name: Bijoy Singh Dighi
mustVisit.description: A roughly 37-acre historic tank in front of the Feni Circuit House, its high tree-lined banks made for pedal-boating and kingfisher-spotting. One of the district's most storied dighis and a favourite afternoon spot.
mustVisit.history: Attributed to Vijay Sen, founder of Bengal's Sen dynasty; local legend says it was dug five or six centuries ago and that its 'holy water' once cured the blindness of a Tripura king's daughter.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 2 km west of Feni town, Feni Sadar

tips: Combine with a Circuit House visit

mustVisit.name: Chand Gazi Bhuiyan Jame Mosque
mustVisit.description: A three-domed Mughal-era mosque with twelve minarets and floral wall reliefs, built in burnt brick with a marble interior floor — a protected national archaeological monument.
mustVisit.history: Built between roughly 1635 and 1700 by Chandgazi Bhuiyan, a Mughal-recognised tax collector and zamindar whose estate reached the Tripura foothills; gazetted as a protected monument in 1987.
tips: Dress modestly; ask before photographing inside
Combine with Shamsher Gazi's country in the same upazila

mustVisit.name: Rajajhi Dighi
mustVisit.description: Feni town's central historic tank at the Zero Point junction — the pond around which the town itself grew, tree-lined and central, with courts and offices on its banks.
mustVisit.history: When the Feni subdivision formed in 1875, the courts, DC office and Court Mosque rose around this dighi; folklore again ties it to a Tripura king who dug it to cure his daughter (his 'ji') — hence 'Raja-jhi'.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: Central Feni town (Zero Point), Feni Sadar

tips: An easy on-foot stop in town
Sweet shops cluster nearby — good for a snack

mustVisit.name: Sharshadi Shahi Mosque (Takiyah Mosque)
mustVisit.description: A three-domed lime-and-brick mosque with walls some five feet thick and vine-and-leaf ornament, known locally as the Takiyah Mosque — tied to the earliest independent Sultanate of Bengal.
mustVisit.history: Associated with Sultan Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah, founder of Bengal's first independent Sultanate, who is said to have made Sharshadi a second capital and built dams, mosques and tombs across the area.
tips: Modest dress; visit outside prayer times

mustVisit.name: Shamsher Gazi Dighi & Fort Site
mustVisit.description: A large historic dighi and fort/palace site near the Feni river and Raghunandan hills, tied to the 18th-century folk hero Shamsher Gazi — a pilgrimage for anyone drawn to regional history.
mustVisit.history: Shamsher Gazi (1712–1760), the 'Tiger of Bhati,' rose from rent-collector to ruler of parts of Tripura/Roshnabad and led a peasant resistance; he kept his main fort at Champaknagar in present Chhagalnaiya.
tips: Signage is sparse — ask locals for directions
Combine with the Chand Gazi mosque nearby

specialties.name: Khondoler Misti
specialties.description: Feni's signature sweet — a rasogolla-style mishti unusual for being served both hot and cold. It originated in Khandal near Parshuram some fifty years ago and is now made by hundreds of families.
specialties.venue: Parshuram (the original 'Khondoler' shop) & Feni-town sweet shops

specialties.name: Feni Sweetmeats
specialties.description: Feni town is known regionally for traditional milk-based sweets; the long-running shops cluster around the Zero Point and Rajajhi Dighi.

specialties.name: Mezban Beef
specialties.description: The greater-Chittagong communal beef feast (mezban) tradition is observed in Feni too — best eaten at a community event rather than a fixed venue.
specialties.venue: Community mezban events across the district

bucketlist.title: Watch sunset over the Muhuri sluice
bucketlist.detail: A 40-gate regulator where three rivers meet, with Bangladesh's first wind turbines turning above the water — the district's best picnic and sunset spot.

bucketlist.title: Pedal-boat on Bijoy Singh Dighi
bucketlist.detail: A 37-acre Sen-dynasty tank wrapped in legend, its tree-lined banks a favourite Feni afternoon.

bucketlist.title: Count the twelve minarets of Chand Gazi Mosque
bucketlist.detail: A burnt-brick Mughal mosque of the 17th century with three domes and twelve minarets — a protected monument in Chhagalnaiya.

bucketlist.title: Eat Khondoler misti hot and cold
bucketlist.detail: Feni's signature sweet from Khandal near Parshuram — a rasogolla-style mishti served both ways.

bucketlist.title: Stroll Rajajhi Dighi at Zero Point
bucketlist.detail: The central tank around which Feni town grew in 1875, ringed by courts and offices.

bucketlist.title: Find the Sharshadi Takiyah Mosque
bucketlist.detail: A three-domed Sultanate-era mosque with five-foot walls, tied to Bengal's first independent sultan.

bucketlist.title: Walk Shamsher Gazi's country
bucketlist.detail: The dighi and fort of the 18th-century 'Tiger of Bhati,' who rose from rent-collector to rule parts of Tripura.

bucketlist.title: See the Maitri Setu border bridge
bucketlist.detail: The 1.9-km Maitri Setu over the Feni river links Bangladesh to Sabroom in Tripura — a new India–Bangladesh crossing.

bucketlist.title: Remember Zahir Raihan in Sonagazi
bucketlist.detail: The Sonagazi upazila gave Bangladesh the filmmaker behind 'Jibon Theke Neya' and 'Stop Genocide' — born at Majupur village.

bucketlist.title: Stroll Kazirbagh Eco Park
bucketlist.detail: A small green park in Feni Sadar with deer, monkeys and peacocks — an easy in-town breather.

bucketlist.title: Pass through the Mohipal bus hub
bucketlist.detail: Feni's highway crossroads on the Dhaka–Chittagong road — the pulse of the town's comings and goings.

bucketlist.title: Eat at a Feni mezban
bucketlist.detail: The greater-Chittagong communal beef feast — rich, spicy and shared, if you can catch a community event.

famousPeople.name: Zahir Raihan
famousPeople.knownFor: Pioneering novelist and filmmaker — director of 'Jibon Theke Neya' (1970) and the 1971 documentary 'Stop Genocide,' and author of 'Hajar Bachhor Dhore.' Born in Majupur village of Sonagazi, Feni; he disappeared in January 1972.

famousPeople.name: Selim Al Deen
famousPeople.knownFor: Eminent playwright and a founding figure of modern Bangla theatre, long a professor at Jahangirnagar University. Born in Shenerkhil village of Sonagazi, Feni.

famousPeople.name: Shamsher Gazi
famousPeople.knownFor: Eighteenth-century folk hero and zamindar, the 'Tiger of Bhati,' who rose from rent-collector to rule parts of Tripura and Roshnabad and led a peasant resistance. Born in Kungura village of Chhagalnaiya, Feni.

didYouKnow: Feni is one of the smallest districts in Bangladesh (~928 sq km) and the smallest in Chittagong division by area.
It became a full district only in 1984 — Bangladesh's 64th — after a century as a subdivision of Noakhali.
The Muhuri Project hosts Bangladesh's first wind-power plant — four turbines installed in 2004–05.
Bijoy Singh Dighi's legend ties it to the Sen dynasty and to a Tripura king's daughter cured by its 'holy water.'
Feni borders India's Tripura, and the 1.9-km Maitri Setu (opened 2021) crosses the Feni river toward Sabroom — though its Bangladesh bridgehead sits just over in Ramgarh.
Feni Junction became a railway junction in 1929, when the line toward Belonia (and Agartala) was built.
